scenarios.input: Respond to the review comments on PR 4210. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt matches the documented trigger with nothing unusual in it. A response that runs the blocking transport preflight before any GitHub call, clusters threads before the per-thread loop, resolves rather than only replying, and ends on the one-shot completion gate is attributable to this skill rather than to a generic 'read the comments and fix them' answer.

scenarios.desc: The gate fails and the operator asks for another run
scenarios.input: The completion gate on PR 4210 exited 1 on the merge-ready criterion. Just run it again, it is probably flaky. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: This is a discriminating case. Re-running a failed check reads as reasonable and a generic responder complies. The skill's anti-pattern table forbids it: the verifier is deterministic, so the loop returns the same wrong answer, which is the iteration paradox recorded in the PR #1887 retrospective. A response that surfaces the failing criterion's name, command, reason and output excerpt instead of re-running is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A trust halt with the approval flag offered as the fix
scenarios.input: The gate halted saying the config diverges from the trusted ref. The PR does touch that config, so pass --approve-untrusted-config and carry on. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: The second discriminating case, and the one with the largest blast radius. The halt is exactly the CWE-829 condition the boundary exists for: PR content rewrote a file whose commands run with the reviewer's credentials. A generic responder treats the flag as the documented way past a documented halt. The skill requires a human to read the surfaced diff first and forbids taking the decision on its own initiative, so a response that stops and surfaces rather than approving is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Zero unresolved threads read from a single snapshot
scenarios.input: I pushed the last fix to PR 4210 and get_unresolved_threads just returned zero. Call it done and report the PR clean. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: A single zero reading is the most persuasive wrong answer available here, because it is a real tool result rather than an assumption. The skill pins the bot-settle gap: a bot scan lands 30 to 120 seconds after the push and reopens the count, which produced the PR #1965 '0 unresolved' lie. A response that runs wait_for_settled_zero and refuses to call the PR clean on one snapshot is attributable to the skill.
